intro: An OCI (Overseas Citizen of India) card photo must be square - width and height equal - not less than 51x51mm, on a plain light-colored background that is explicitly not white, with no border. For the online application's digital upload, the official FAQ specifies 200-900 pixels (width and height equal) as JPEG/JPG, under 200KB.

This tool crops your photo to exactly 51x51mm at 300 DPI - 602x602 pixels, comfortably inside the official 200-900px digital range - and compresses it under the 200KB ceiling. This is a digital-upload-only document, so the print-sheet export isn't offered for it.

faqs.q: What size is an OCI card photo?
faqs.a: Square, not less than 51x51mm physically; for the online application's digital upload, 200-900 pixels (equal width and height), per OCI Services' official FAQ.

faqs.q: What background color is required?
faqs.a: A plain, light-colored background - the official FAQ explicitly says "not white," without naming a specific alternative color. A light grey or pastel tone is a safe interpretation.

faqs.q: Is there a file size limit?
faqs.a: Yes - 200KB maximum, in JPEG/JPG format, per the official FAQ. That's stricter than most other documents this tool supports.

faqs.q: How tall should my face be in the photo?
faqs.a: The official FAQ says "80% coverage of face" without a precise chin-to-crown millimeter figure; several third-party guides cite 25-33mm, which is more consistent with how a 51x51mm frame is typically proportioned (matching this tool's US template, the same physical size). This tool's alignment guide follows that more specific figure - treat it as a close approximation and check your result against the official page.

faqs.q: Can I get this photo printed for a physical application?
faqs.a: The specification we sourced is for the online application's digital upload. This tool doesn't offer a print-sheet export for this document since the online process is digital-only - check current OCI application instructions if a physical photo is separately required in your case.

faqs.q: Can I smile in the photo?
faqs.a: No - a neutral expression with mouth closed is expected, consistent with the biometric-style photo rules most Indian government documents share.
